blocks.heading: What today is
blocks.body: About 90 minutes. Do the lab in the app. The check at the end uses words from today only.

blocks.heading: Sites console
blocks.body:
The **Sites** console is where the website team’s page tree lives. Create, copy, move, properties. Official docs call the literacy **Basic Handling** :  how you move around, select, and open.

It is not Maps Manager. Do not look for a topicref, a key, or completeness here.

Kitepump is still your training product. Their landing page for it would live in this tree. Your handbook still lives in Oxygen.

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
This lab can fail. Fail when: The log calls the Sites tree a ditamap, or the mock includes Oxygen toolbars, or there are zero official-video notes.

Expected: Three control names from the video. Tree vs booklet sentence. Mock labeled.

blocks.intro: Walk the steps in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: Watch the official Quick site creation video. Pause on the Sites console (or the closest view). Write three control names you can see.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: Open samples/aem-author-field-log/mocks/sites-console.txt. It is a labeled mock, not a screenshot of Adobe UI.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: Write oxygen-bootcamp-work/week9/field-log-57.txt: Sites console is a page tree. A DITA map is a booklet of topics. They do not share a toolbar.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: List three jobs: go to a folder, open a page’s properties, open a page for edit. Write ‘verify in your version’ next to any guessed label.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.body: Do not draw Oxygen Maps Manager inside the mock.

blocks.summary: Three control names from the video. Tree vs booklet sentence. Mock labeled.

blocks.q: You need to find the Kitepump landing page on the website team’s desk. First surface?
blocks.why: Pages live in Sites. Booklets live in Oxygen. Two trees. Two apps.

blocks.q: The Sites tree and your booklet both look like lists. Why not treat them as the same thing?
options: Sites holds web pages. A map holds pointers to help-page files. Different files, different toolbar
blocks.why: A tree is a tree. The thing in it is not. Do not look for topicref here.

blocks.q: Card view, column view, list view. Why care?
options: They are ways to see the same page tree :  pick one and still know it is not your booklet
blocks.why: Views are views. The tree is still Sites.
